newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River restrictions remain in place.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River restrictions remain in place.

text.p: Shipping restrictions remained in place on Thursday along a 100-mile stretch of the Mississippi River as crews worked to remove a capsized barge from the site of Monday's accident near here, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
Shipping is restricted to one-way traffic along the river from milepost 329.3 to milepost 233.9 upstream from Baton Rouge, Coast Guard Petty Officer Tyler Johnson said.
"The safety zone will remain in place until salvage operations are complete," he said.

The river just north of Baton Rouge was closed Monday after a tow with 25 barges hit a bridge, sinking two rock barges and capsizing a tanker barge carrying a mix of gasoline and benzene. The river was reopened to one-way traffic Wednesday afternoon with restrictions overnight.
Crews are expected to begin lightering the sunken barge on Thursday.
In addition to hampering the flow of vessels on the river, the barge accident forced the indefinite closure of two gambling riverboats, the Belle of Baton Rouge and Casino Rouge.
